result.title: Look Before You Commit: Visual-Evidence-Guided Decoding for Multimodal Diffusion Language Models
result.summary: Diffusion multimodal large language models rely on confidence to decide when to commit candidate tokens during generation. In multimodal tasks, however, confidence cannot distinguish whether a candidate originates from image evidence or the language prior. We perform paired forward ablation and find that nearly nine out of ten high-confidence commits are insensitive to the image, while degenerate and hallucination samples exhibit significant increases in the entropy of deep-layer attention organization. Based on this diagnosis, we propose CD-APC, a training-free decoding method. CD-APC performs evidence-adjusted scoring within a base-supported pool and uses dual gating based on model acceptability and contrastive concentration to decide whether to commit, together with an inverse-window mechanism that adapts to inter-step difficulty. Across two backbones and five benchmarks, CD-APC consistently improves performance, indicating that stable visual evidence improves model outputs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断多模态扩散语言模型中「置信度无法区分候选来自图像证据还是语言先验」的问题：通过配对前向消融发现近九成高置信提交对图像不敏感，且幻觉样本深层注意力组织熵升高；据此提出免训练的 CD-APC 解码，在证据校正打分、可接受性与对比集中度双重门控下决定是否提交候选。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 LVR 中「何时提交（STOP）应以视觉证据为依据」及视觉旁路、证据筛选问题，其消融诊断与提交门控可供核查 latent 状态是否真正使用视觉信息；但方法作用于 token 级扩散解码，与内部 latent 推理状态的映射仍需阅读原文确认。
